title: Atrial fibrillation effector gene predictions (Roselli et al., 2018)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

Multi-ethnic genome-wide association study for atrial fibrillation.
Roselli C, et al.
Nat Genet. 2018 Sep;50(9):1225-1233. doi: 10.1038/s41588-018-0133-9.
PMID: 29892015

At each atrial fibrillation (AF) associated locus, genes were prioritized as potentially causal for AF based on six criteria:

  • proximity to the signal (Nearest Gene)
  • GTEx Heart Expression (left ventricle and atrial appendage): genes are listed if within 500KB of the sentinel variant and gene expression for at least one heart tissue in GTEx is in the top 5 and median (RMPK) > 1
  • Genes within enriched pathways: genes are listed if within 500kb of sentinel variant and present in at least one enriched pathway as identified by gene set enrichment analysis
  • eQTL MAGNet Left Atrial: listed genes are eGenes for eQTLs in left atrial tissue from the Myocardial Applied Genomics Network (MAGNet) repository that overlap with atrial fibrillation GWAS signals
  • eQTL GTEx Heart (left ventricle and atrial appendage): listed genes are eGenes for eQTLs in left ventricle and atrial appendage from GTEx that overlap with atrial fibrillation GWAS signals
  • MetaXcan Heart (left ventricle and atrial appendage): genes whose transcription level in heart left ventricle and atrial appendage is predicted by MetaXcan analysis to be associated with AF disease risk
